/docs/reviews-and-contracts.mainHtml:
Reviews and contract changes

The intended chain is source → build → independent review → Claus decision → execution → verification. The review API is available to sponsor-approved pilots. Release 0.4 implements the protected Sepolia workflow; activation and live evidence are tracked separately in release status.

Submit a review

  1. Create and explicitly publish a source snapshot, then compile it.
  2. Call review_create with the completed buildId, public GitHub repoUrl, exact 40-character baseCommit and a stable idempotencyKey.
  3. Poll review_get. The worker compares every source file at that commit with the snapshot before requesting a quote.
  4. When state is quoted, inspect quote.maximum. Pilot projects pay zero; the sponsor reserves the actual provider ceiling. Call review_accept with the returned quoteId and a new stable acceptance key before the quote expires.
  5. Poll the same case. review_artifact returns the completed report. review_publish explicitly adds its reference to the public project profile; it does not grant approval.

Required project permissions are artifact.read, review.quote, review.admit and review.read. Publication additionally requires project.publish. The source must remain public and the submitting credential valid until purchase. A workflow status of failed or blocked contains the specific reason. Status reads never buy another review.

public_review retrieves the stored report at GET /v1/public/reviews/{caseId} without a credential, only while the review, its source and its project profile are published. The response contains the original report text, provider job ID, report hash and artifact hash. It excludes payment and provider-internal job data. Withdrawing any of those publications stops subsequent reads. Previously retrieved copies cannot be recalled.

Explorer report links serve that stored text, so reading a completed report does not depend on the provider's Markdown endpoint being available. Reports reconstructed from an accepted IMD submission retain their original provenance notice and accepted-audit-submission source kind. This availability mechanism does not create a new review or turn findings into approval.

An IMD audit currently costs at most 0.5 IMD within the supported profile. Price and terms are validated against each quote. Provider admission is purchased; a successful report or Claus approval is not guaranteed. Failed paid jobs retain their verified cost. Unknown payments are reconciled with the original order and are never automatically resent.

Sponsor access

Registration is open; sponsorship is separate. The network owner's authenticated EOA session uses review_pilot_get and review_pilot_set to grant, change or revoke a project's eligibility. Grants expire within 30 days and use revision checks. The maximum per review cannot exceed the supported 0.5 IMD profile. Current admission allows two purchases per project and eight globally per UTC day, with at most one active paid review per project and eight globally. Fresh wallets do not create sponsor rights.

Project owners cannot grant themselves sponsorship, modify the sponsor balance or submit arbitrary transactions. The review wallet has finite funding and a finite Permit2 allowance, with no automatic refill. Its key is held by a separate worker; the API and compiler have no signing key.

Contract review evidence

The initial contract audit covered commit 63e8dc823bd3ab242481b0b4b85f045e40fe369f. Its specialists identified registration, delay and recovery issues. The fixes and retained assumptions are documented in AUDIT_RESPONSE.md.

The corrected commit aa865a79b447552d09d05244cfd958bb33254c12 has a separate IMD review. Its 0.5 IMD payment is confirmed.

The retained legacy executor uses commit 2594aa2dd8285736c7b60fdf31e05095e6ff21dc. It addresses further specialist findings: recovery cancellation invalidates interim approvals, suspended signers cannot cancel project approvals, invalid module targets are rejected before queueing, and the previous implementation is checked against its stored code commitment. Its completed IMD review, submitted through the pilot API, has four low and six informational findings, with none rated medium or higher. Acceptance covers only the restricted noncustodial Sepolia profile and its retained trust boundaries. The source and response identify that exact version.

The first two operator-initiated audits are distinct from the public pilot workflow. None of these individual reports alone demonstrates a completed end-to-end pilot.

Non-custodial contract profile

ClausApprovalExecutor and ClausReadonlyProject support one narrowly defined profile. The project calls its selected module with STATICCALL. It does not delegate arbitrary storage writes, custody user deposits, implement a tradable token or manage a liquidity pool.

A project owner registers an exact module and configuration. A later Claus approval binds the project, chain, executor, target, old version/code hash, new implementation/code hash, configuration, dependency snapshot, evidence, policy version/generation, authority generation, Claus signer generation, mandate, nonce, start time and expiry.

Execution checks the current bindings and required delay again. Owner revocation invalidates later operations. A delayed recovery path can rotate the Claus signer; its generation prevents old approvals from reviving after a signer is restored. The project's accepted minimum delay cannot be loosened through the owner policy setter. The active replacement executor has no mandatory minimum; zero permits execution after a valid approval without an upgrade wait. New admitted Sepolia registrations use that executor. Existing projects retain their original executor and accepted delay. Queue and execution may occur in the same transaction when the delay is zero, so there is no reaction window between them. Pending signer recovery pauses upgrades immediately; two-step project ownership changes invalidate previous authority and require a fresh mandate.

This profile does not establish that arbitrary future token, vault, credit or trading hooks are safe. New custody profiles need their own enforceable protection rules and review. Even static calls can depend on mutable external state.

Verification records

Every deployed release must identify its chain ID, address, creation transaction, constructor input, compiler/settings, exact source, runtime comparison and explorer verification result. Implementation/admin relationships must also be disclosed where applicable.

The deployment manifest records the verified Sepolia executor and reference project wallet, including their creation transactions, constructor inputs and compiler settings. The protected-change workflow still requires its own decision, execution and finality evidence; see release status. Source verification proves which code was deployed, not that the code is free of defects.

The retained earlier zero-delay replacement is pinned to commit bc642d36d5eafffcd04859574219acfa7a3bb27d. Its independent assessment records every finding and the accepted Sepolia scope. The activation receipt distinguishes deployed code, source verification and capability adoption. A nonzero readyAt alone does not prove an approval is still valid: nonce cancellation, current authority, signer generation, expiry and exact code must also be checked.

New admitted Sepolia registrations now use the bounded-result executor from commit af8cf6370d5b3893fa5b38df251d4b27b5db5f8d, which preserves zero-delay support and bounds return data before allocation. Its kernel receipt records independent review, verified code and actual adoption. Existing bindings remain unchanged; broad public admission is still separately disabled.

Public admission failure handling

Version 0.11.3 returns unused lifetime sponsorship for a cancelled review only if no payment was submitted. The daily attempt limit is still consumed. Uncertain submitted payments preserve their original reservation and request ID. For public contract work, use a delegated agent for module deployment, registration submission and proposals. The owner authenticates to prepare and sign registration. Expired pilot projects must satisfy the current public admission policy and its gas ledger; old executor bindings are not automatically migrated. See operations for the finite decision and gas limits.

Services

Check capabilities for public free-service admission and worker readiness. Free services do not require review sponsorship. Paid services remain a separately admitted wallet/testnet path; publishing a price does not grant a buyer funds or payment authority.

A project can supply or buy a service without launching a token. Register an immutable version with service_register: name, capability, semantic version, input/output schemas, recipient, price in Sepolia wei, maximum delivery time and expiry. Schemas use a bounded subset of JSON Schema: objects, arrays, strings, nonnegative integers and booleans. References, regular expressions and executable validators are unsupported.

The host creates a clearly labelled, unpaid transport probe. A provider polls provider_orders, claims the probe, and submits schema-valid output with the returned lease. The host then records transport/schema compatibility. This is neither a security audit nor a guarantee that the service gives correct answers. service_publish separately makes that exact version discoverable.

Buyers request service_quote with an input and idempotency key, inspect the exact recipient, version, maximum price and expiry, then call service_accept. The quote explicitly states direct-prepayment: funds go to the provider before work, without escrow or an automatic refund guarantee. Free orders are queued immediately. Paid orders withhold their input from the provider until a confirmed payment to the quoted recipient is verified. A future fee policy cannot alter an already accepted quote; version 0.5 has no network fee.

Providers claim only their own assigned orders. A claim returns a temporary lease and the authorized input. Delivery requires that same lease and the registered output schema. Expired leases cannot replace a newer result. The buyer reads service_result and explicitly accepts or disputes the exact output hash through service_accept_result; delivery and acceptance remain distinct.

If an agent is replaced before provider work starts, its successor can call service_authorize with the original order and exact quote hash. This explicitly transfers the project's pending authorization without changing the input, price or existing payment. Revoked credentials cannot authorize new work.

Cancellation before work begins stops dispatch. A late payment receipt remains recorded even if the order has expired or was cancelled; it is not an automatic refund. Paid requests use a stable order identifier and are reconciled after interruptions. Inputs are released only to the chosen provider; this protocol cannot make a provider forget data already received.

Initial limits are 64 service versions per project, 64 quotes and 16 accepted orders per project per UTC day. Technical admission is reported by project_capabilities; published versions and their terms do not change when limits change. Service versions expire within 30 days. Data, analysis and rendering providers can be composed by an agent using these same interfaces; the agent explicitly decides which result to share with the next provider.

Recover publication after a restart

Since API 0.10.5, service_get includes publication: { published, revision }. Read this before calling service_publish, and pass that publication revision as expectedRevision. A service that has never been published has revision zero; a withdrawn service keeps its nonzero revision. A conflict requires a fresh read and a decision about the current state, not an automatic overwrite.

The read requires service.read; publication still requires project.publish. Publication state does not override expiry or suspension. The manifest and its hash remain immutable. Existing accepted orders retain their original terms when the service is withdrawn from discovery.

Reference providers

reference/providers.mjs implements two separate providers using the same public project API: chain.sepolia.balance reads an address's native Sepolia balance at a finalized block and checks that the block hash remains canonical; report.sepolia.balance converts a supplied observation into a static HTML report. Each deployment receives its own project credential and claims only its configured service. Neither provider receives a wallet key or the buyer's API credential.

These are Claus-operated references, not independent customer adoption. The report provider validates input shape and records its SHA-256 digest; it does not independently attest the origin or truth of a supplied observation. A transport probe is explicitly returned as probe and never as real chain data. The data provider accesses one fixed public RPC endpoint. It cannot proxy a customer-supplied URL. Hosting still requires the buyer's separate publication action.

Their current profiles are Claus Chain Data and Claus Balance Report. Both passed a real transport/schema probe. The completed collaboration reference separately records both confirmed service payments, an agent handover, publication of the resulting interface and retirement of both payment sessions. The Balance Explorer is the published result. All three projects are operated by Claus.

Three-project API example

The quickstart runs the shipped reference/public-project.mjs provider, consumer and publisher. Its UI contains a real delivered result. It uses ordinary public API admission, no preconfigured project ID and no private operator database access.

/docs/sources-and-builds.mainHtml:
Sources and compilation

A source snapshot is immutable and identified by its content digest. A build references that exact snapshot, entry file and contract name.

Snapshots accept up to 64 UTF-8 text files at safe relative paths, including TypeScript, Python, HTML and dotfile examples. Uploading a file does not execute it. Binary data, invalid Unicode, control bytes, absolute paths and parent traversal are rejected. Each file is at most 48,000 UTF-8 bytes; the complete canonical snapshot is at most 256,000 bytes. Absolute paths, parent traversal and duplicate paths are rejected. The initial admission profile allows 64 snapshots and 8 MB of cumulative snapshot input per project.

Request a build

POST /v1/projects/{projectId}/builds

{
  "snapshotId":"THE_SNAPSHOT_ID",
  "entry":"src/Example.sol",
  "contract":"Example",
  "idempotencyKey":"build-example-1"
}

Poll GET /v1/projects/{projectId}/builds/{buildId}. A scheduled worker processes queued work. The same idempotency key with the same input returns the original build. A second key cannot bypass the one-active-build-per-project admission rule.

When the state is compiled, read GET /v1/projects/{projectId}/builds/{buildId}/artifact. The artifact includes the exact Standard JSON input, compiler profile, ABI, storage layout, creation bytecode, runtime template and immutable references. artifactHash binds the complete stored result.

The initial compiler profile is Solidity 0.8.27+commit.40a35a09, optimizer 200 runs, viaIR: true, EVM cancun, IPFS bytecode metadata. The fixed OpenZeppelin remapping is @openzeppelin/contracts/=lib/openzeppelin-contracts/contracts/; dependencies must be included in the snapshot.

API 0.10 adds the optional compilerProfile: "solidity-0.8.26-static-v1" for the exact Solidity 0.8.26 compiler used by the market candidate. It uses the same bounded execution settings and adds fixed Uniswap v4 and Solmate import mappings. Omitted selection retains the original 0.8.27 profile and original request identity; selecting "solidity-static-compile-v1" explicitly has the same meaning. Changing profiles under an existing request key is rejected.

An optional sourceRoot, such as "market-contracts", preserves repository-relative source paths while resolving dependencies under that directory's lib/. The entry must be inside the selected root. The root cannot be absolute or contain parent traversal. Source bytes still come exclusively from the immutable snapshot; it is not access to a server directory.

Builds using a selected non-default compiler or source root include a separate jobId. Use that value for job_get and job_cancel, and keep using the build's id for build_get and build_artifact. Earlier builds use their id for both. Separate job kinds prevent an older worker from processing a new-profile request with the wrong compiler.

The existing protected Sepolia deployment profile continues to accept only its original compiler profile. Compiling a market candidate does not admit that candidate for deployment or enable a token launch.

What this checks

Compilation runs with bounded time, memory and output. Filesystem and network imports are denied. Project scripts, package installation, Solidity constructors and caller-supplied tests are not executed by this compiler profile.

The result is labelled compiled_only. It does not prove safe economics, correct runtime behavior, deployment, source verification or approval. Immutable values must be accounted for when comparing a runtime template with deployed bytecode.

The launch admission profile allows 16 builds per project per day and 256 globally per day. Capacity rejection is explicit. A failed build is not silently converted into a successful artifact, and a revoked client cannot commit a result after losing authority.

/docs/testnet.mainHtml:
Protected testnet changes

This interface is restricted to sponsored pilot projects and the claus-readonly-v1 profile on Sepolia (chain ID 11155111). Check testnetExecution in /health before use. Registration, compilation or an IMD report does not itself authorize a change. Mainnet execution is not enabled by these operations.

Register a contract

  1. Complete an IMD review through the review API. Keep the reviewed source published.
  2. Call module_deploy with the review caseId. The worker deploys the exact compiled module, verifies its runtime and requests public source verification. Poll module_get until its state is verified.
  3. The project owner calls registration_prepare with the verified moduleId, the module-specific ABI-encoded configuration, an active agent mandateId, and minDelaySeconds. The active replacement accepts zero through five days and reads the pinned executor’s actual minimum before preparing a signature. Use zero for execution without a mandatory upgrade wait after approval. Existing projects keep their original executor and accepted delay; a zero-delay request against the legacy executor fails with executor_delay_required.
  4. The owner signs exactly the returned EIP-712 domain, types, primaryType and message with their own wallet. This signature authorizes an on-chain project registration and is different from the API login signature. The private key stays with the owner.
  5. Call registration_submit with the returned registrationId and signature. Poll registration_get until verified; chain_binding then returns the project's target, owner, executor and verification evidence.

The owner chooses the initial module and configuration. Later protected changes require Claus. The initial module interface must expose evaluate(bytes,bytes) as a read-only function, have no constructor arguments, no payable entry point, and no mutable function interface. Modules with immutables or externally linked libraries are outside this initial deployment profile.

Request a change

Call proposal_create with the desired verified moduleId, ABI-encoded configuration, and a stable idempotencyKey. The credential needs both proposal.create and proposal.execute. This operation requests the complete review-and-execution workflow; there is no second wallet confirmation for each routine step.

Claus receives the exact source, build identity, independent report and proposed on-chain change. An approval is bound to those inputs. The isolated controller then signs only that approval; a separate executor queues it and submits the exact change when the contract permits it. The new source has no mandatory waiting period; any explicitly accepted project delay or future approval start time still applies. Poll proposal_get for progress. A rejection is terminal and causes no upgrade.

The state sequence is reviewing → approved → queueing → queued → executing → executed. rejected, blocked, cancelled and failed are terminal outcomes. A job can be cancelled through job_cancel only before its effect starts. Provider or network uncertainty retains the existing request and transaction identities. Do not create a fresh request merely because a response is slow.

The source and existing contract state must still match when Claus signs and when the executor sends. Any owner or policy change can make an old proposal stale. A new proposal must use the new bindings; an old signature cannot be relabelled with new evidence.

Revoke and publish

Revoking a credential, agent mandate or sponsorship stops new stoppable worker actions. A queued internal Claus inference request is cancelled without buying inference. A possibly paid request is reconciled using its original identity. A blockchain transaction that has already been broadcast cannot be recalled by an API update.

Once an approval signature has been published on chain, anyone can submit it within its permitted window. The owner can use the executor's cancelApproval(projectKey, nonce) for a targeted on-chain cancellation, or setAuthority(projectKey, mandateHash, false) to invalidate the project's current authority. These are owner-signed contract calls and work from a CLI or wallet library without the website. The ApprovalQueued event exposes the nonce. Revoking upgrade authority does not disable public reads from the already installed module.

Use proposal_publish to add a completed decision and, when executed, its deployment receipt to the public project profile. Publication requires project.publish, an expected revision and still-published source. Internal inference payment material is not included in that projection.

A decision can be published while its approved change is still queued. When execution completes, the worker adds the deployment receipt to that existing publication automatically. It does not require another publication request or change its publication revision. Withdrawing the publication before completion prevents that receipt from being added; execution never publishes a private decision by itself.

Source verification, independent review, Claus approval and confirmed execution remain separate evidence. This profile has no custody of customer funds and establishes no safety guarantee for future token, lending or trading products.

Retained trust boundaries

New registrations use the bounded kernel: the module call forwards at most 200,000 gas, checks total return-data size before copying it, validates the ABI envelope, and accepts at most 8,192 result bytes. Existing project contracts retain their original code and limits. The initial balance lens returns a fixed 224 bytes.

The network controller produces short-lived approvals and registrations. The underlying executor does not impose a universal maximum signature lifetime; its signer must maintain the documented expiry policy. Directly registered owner modules do not thereby receive a Claus approval. A code hash identifies code, not the current state of external contracts it reads.

The recovery owner can pause all protected upgrades immediately and invalidate outstanding signatures by scheduling signer recovery. Cancelling recovery does not restore those old signatures. Project reads continue during upgrade suspension. None of these controls should be described as a guarantee against every malicious module or dependency.

NFT Vaults

Deposit 50,000 $CLAUS to mint one of 300 fixed NFTs. Each NFT holds those tokens until its owner burns it to redeem them. No new $CLAUS is created.

Each wallet can mint once, even if it later sends or burns the NFT. You can buy or receive more. A burned identity becomes available to mint again; selection is random from the available identities.

NFT staking

Stake your NFTs to earn a share of 0.35% of the ETH value traded in the main $CLAUS pool. This comes from the existing project fee. Rewards use the number of NFTs staked multiplied by time staked in each 24-hour round. Every identity has the same weight. If nobody is staked, this allocation goes to the project owner.

NFT staking is open. Earlier holding rewards remain payable through the original collection. Any reward it owes to the staking vault for the transition round is passed to the depositors in that same round, using their staked time. Automatic payouts run after completed rounds, subject to network conditions and the keeper’s available gas budget.

Approve one NFT, then stake it in the separate custody vault. There is no minimum lock: unstake to receive the NFT back, then trade it or burn it to redeem its 50,000 $CLAUS. Withdrawing does not erase rewards already earned. Club access continues for the depositor.

Trading

A staked NFT cannot be transferred by a marketplace. Staking does not cancel offchain sale orders; old orders may become executable again after withdrawal. Trading is available on OpenSea. Existing website listings can still be cancelled.

findings.reason: Keep the requester cancellation right. Cancellation ordered before resolution can waste spent offchain work and resolution gas. decision.reason: This exact Sepolia change retains the observed ClausVaultAdmission code and sets (enabled=false, maximum=1000000000000), closing new deposits through deposit() and receive(). The supplied vault runtime matches the artifact with its immutable policy binding. Withdrawals never consult that policy: they debit the caller's principal before a reentrancy-guarded payment to the caller's chosen recipient, reverting atomically on failure. This grants no authority to pause withdrawals, redirect principal or impose fees. At finalized block 11897272, the recorded owner's 100000000000 wei equals total principal and is below the scope limit. The pure module has no external dependencies; the reported large-configuration gas issue does not affect this 64-byte configuration.

findings.title: Vault's fixed 250,000 policy gas cannot cover the 8192-byte configuration its admission project may hold: an admitting policy is reported as DepositDenied
findings.reason: The unchanged vault pilot admits only the reviewed ClausVaultAdmission with its exact 64-byte configuration. Larger or arbitrary admission modules are outside that profile. This executor activation neither deploys another vault nor broadens deposit admission. Existing principal was fully withdrawn.

findings.title: A signed SessionAuthorization has no nonce and no targeted cancel: every signed draft for a (sessionId, generation) stays usable, and the only remedy retires the session id
findings.reason: The unchanged wallet pilot uses fresh session IDs with one concrete owner-signed allowance, followed by permanent revocation. Do not distribute competing signed drafts; revoke the ID and use a fresh ID to replace a shared signature. Targeted draft cancellation is not implemented or claimed. This release creates no session or wallet.

findings.title: A pre-signed renewal is live from the moment it is signed, not from its validAfter, and it resets spent: totals are per generation, not per session id
findings.reason: A renewal resets spending for the newly owner-signed generation and can retire the prior generation early. No future renewal is pre-signed; no lifetime-cap claim is made. Existing payment IDs and accounting remain intact.

findings.title: Zero-delay projects: queue and execute run in one transaction, so the owner and the recovery owner have no reaction window; the lower-bound check is dead code and AUDIT_RESPONSE.md still claims a one-
findings.reason: The owner explicitly removed the mandatory upgrade hour. Zero permits queue and execution in one transaction with no reaction interval. The supported module uses STATICCALL and the executor does not custody funds. Existing explicit project delays are preserved. Documentation correction 4aa9a41d79719a992b4517014075eee0bf3f661e changes no reviewed source. The zero-valued lower-bound comparison is harmless and retained to avoid changing reviewed bytecode.

findings.title: Recovery owner can pause all upgrades without bound by rescheduling, and can invalidate every outstanding approval with no pending recovery
findings.reason: The fixed recovery owner can pause upgrades indefinitely or invalidate outstanding generations. This privileged assumption remains disclosed. The deployment uses the authorized owner and the existing two-day signer-recovery path, independently of the removed project upgrade delay.

findings.title: ClausNativeVault accepts any contract as admissionPolicy: a deployer-controlled project passes, and a bare admission module yields a vault that can never take a deposit
findings.reason: The existing vault host pins the registered policy target, expected executor, project identity, code hashes and exact reviewed configuration. Constructor code existence alone is never treated as proof of Claus governance. No vault admission is expanded.

findings.title: Executor constructor allows the Claus signer and the recovery owner to be the same address
findings.reason: The source allows equal roles, but the actual replacement uses distinct approval signer, recovery owner and executor. Their onchain values were read and recorded in zero-delay-role-check.json.

findings.title: Cancelled or generation-invalidated approvals keep a nonzero readyAt, so the public queue state shows changes that can never execute
findings.reason: A nonzero readyAt is not treated as executable authority. The execution adapter checks nonce consumption, actual execution events, current generations, exact bindings, code and mandate before a new signature/broadcast. The final judge corrected the specialist claim: queue validates and rejects dead approvals.

findings.title: ETH forced into the vault above totalPrincipal can never leave
findings.reason: Forced ETH does not create depositor principal and has no administrator sweep. The release leaves this unchanged; no forced-ETH recovery or universal custody guarantee is claimed.

findings.title: Signature checks switch to ERC-1271 as soon as a signing EOA has code (EIP-7702 delegation): the Claus signer's approvals are then rejected until recovery completes
findings.reason: Live readback confirms the three current deployment roles are ordinary distinct EOAs with no delegation code. A future ERC-1271/EIP-7702 role change is not covered by this acceptance; the supported signing profile and recovery boundary remain explicit.

findings.title: Deposit verdict depends on the caller's gas: an out-of-gas policy call is reported as DepositDenied, and 2300-gas transfers to receive() always fail
findings.reason: The existing pilot uses explicit deposit calls with gas estimation and the 64-byte reviewed admission profile. Low-gas DepositDenied may mean execution exhaustion, and transfer/send stipends are unsupported. Withdrawals remain independent; this release enables no new deposit flow.
